title: (II) COSMOGONY: The Kingdom of Light
english_translation:
[R/Hd] shall be in the whole Church

[V/Hd] (and the community of) Righteous- ness

[R] <The first is the great king god Zurwan, father of righteousness. The second, the 12 aeons who stand> before the great king god Zurwan. The third, the blessed places without count and number in which the (5) light gods, angels, mahraspands, and pow- ers dwell, in great bliss and joy. (10) The Fourth, the pure air in the light paradise, wondrous, beautiful to behold: immea- surable (is) its goodness for them. By supernatural power it shall by itself bring into being the god's marvelous (15) dress and garment, throne, diadem, and fragrant wreath, ornaments, and fineries of all sorts. The fifth, the light earth, *self-existent, eternal, (20) miraculous. In *height it is beyond *reach, its *depth cannot be perceived. No enemy and no *injurer walk this earth. Its (25) divine pavement is of the substance of diamond that does not shake forever. All good things are born from it: adorned, graceful hills wholly covered with flowers, grown (30) in much excellence; green fruit-bearing trees whose fruits never *drop, never rot, and never become wormed; [V] springs flowing with ambro- sia (35) that fill the whole paradise; its groves and plans; countless mansions and palaces, thrones and *benches that exist in perpetuity for ever and ever. (40) Thus arranged is the paradise in these five greatnesses. They are calm in quietude and know no fear. They live in the light, where (45) they have no darkness; in eternal life, where they have no death; in health without sickness; in joy, where they have no sorrow; in charity without hatred; in the company of friends, (50) where there is no separation from them; in a shape that is not brought to nought, in a divine body, where

there is no destruction; on ambrosial food without restriction; wherefore (55) they bear no toil and hardship. In appearance they are ornate, in strength powerful, in wealth exceedingly rich; of poverty they know not even the name. Nay they are equipped, (60) beautiful, and embellished; no damage occurs to their bodies. Their garment of joy is finery that never gets soiled, of seventy myriad kinds, set with jewels. (65) Their places are never destroyed ...

editorial_notes: Interleaved Sogdian transliteration and English translation were separated. PDF/OCR running headers and stray pagination were removed. Hyphenation from line breaks in the English (e.g., 'pow- ers', 'immea- surable', 'ambro- sia') was retained as in the OCR. The initial English clause ends mid-sentence ('...in a divine body, where') and resumes only later ('there is no destruction...'); this discontinuity reflects the source excerpt. Ellipsis at the end ('...') preserved.
